title: Agent Speedrun — Elizabeth Fuentes Leone & Sandhya Subramani, AWS
talk_summary: AWS workshop builds a Strands customer-service agent and demonstrates hooks, skills, steering, and AgentCore deployment. The transferable parts are deterministic loop hooks, lazy skill loading, checker-agent steering, and per-run observability; the AWS deployment/marketing is not relevant.

takeaways.technique: Deterministic loop hooks with hard stop
takeaways.what_they_do: Register callbacks before invocation/tool call to count tool calls per user request and block or end the turn when exceeding a max.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can define the hook in such a way to even end the agent's turn

takeaways.what_they_do: A deterministic Python hook inspects input before the LLM call and blocks sensitive data so the model never receives it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the model never is going to receive that information. So you block the call so you don't waste token.

takeaways.what_they_do: Store task playbooks as markdown skill files; the agent reads the skills folder and invokes the relevant skill as a tool only when needed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you don't want to overflow it with all of the amount of information you have because those are also considered input tokens

takeaways.technique: Steering checker agent at hook points
takeaways.what_they_do: Attach a buddy/steering agent at before/after LLM or tool-call points to check and correct output format, tone, or workflow before final response.
takeaways.evidence_quote: your buddy agent is sort of checking and correcting and course correcting

takeaways.what_they_do: Instrument the runtime to trace messages, tool calls, token spend, and agent-loop events per session.
Put many MCP/tools behind one endpoint with semantic search so the agent loop gets the best matching tool rather than all tools.
takeaways.evidence_quote: only one endpoint for all your NCP for all your tools and it have semantic search
